bit.name: advance the state by the step times the current slope
bit.mechanism: from the current state evaluate the rate of change once, move the state by that rate times the step length, and repeat; nothing from earlier steps is kept
requires: a rate function evaluable at any state
a step length (policy)
fails_when: first-order error; unstable on stiff problems unless the step is tiny

bit.name: advance the state by the slope taken at the new point
bit.mechanism: choose the next state so that the rate evaluated AT that next state, times the step, is exactly the move from the current state; each step is therefore an equation to solve, usually by a few fixed-point or Newton iterations
requires: a solver for the per-step implicit equation
fails_when: each step costs a solve; damps genuine oscillations along with instabilities

bit.name: advance the state by the mean of the old and new slopes
bit.mechanism: choose the next state so that the move equals the step times the average of the rate at the current state and the rate at the next state; implicit like the backward step but second-order and non-damping
requires: a solver for the per-step implicit equation
fails_when: oscillatory (not damped) error on very stiff components

bit.name: combine slopes sampled at trial points inside the step
bit.mechanism: evaluate the rate at the current state, use it to reach a trial point part-way through the step, evaluate again there, repeat for a fixed number of stages, and advance by a fixed weighted combination of the sampled slopes chosen so low-order errors cancel
requires: a rate function evaluable at trial states
a tableau of stage weights (data)
fails_when: several rate evaluations per step; explicit forms still fail on stiff problems

bit.name: advance by a fixed linear combination of previous states and slopes
bit.mechanism: keep a window of the last few states and their rates; the next state is a fixed linear combination of them (and, in implicit forms, of its own rate), so only one new rate evaluation is needed per step
requires: a start-up procedure to fill the window
fixed coefficient sets (data)
fails_when: changing the step length invalidates the window; some coefficient sets are unstable

bit.name: advance position from the two previous positions and the acceleration
bit.mechanism: new position = twice the current position minus the previous position plus acceleration times step squared; velocity never appears, the update is time-reversible and conserves an energy-like quantity over long runs
requires: second-order dynamics (acceleration from position only)
fails_when: velocity-dependent forces break the symmetry; step length must be fixed

bit.name: replace derivatives by difference quotients on a grid
bit.mechanism: lay a grid over the domain, replace each derivative in the equation by a difference of neighbouring grid values divided by the spacing, and solve the resulting algebraic system for the grid values
requires: a regular grid
boundary values
fails_when: irregular domains fit badly; error scales with spacing to a low power

bit.name: trade time derivatives for space derivatives via the equation, then difference
bit.mechanism: expand the next time level as a Taylor series in time, use the governing equation to rewrite each time derivative as a space derivative, then replace those by centred differences on the grid; second-order in both time and space
requires: a hyperbolic (wave-like) equation
a step ratio inside the stability bound
fails_when: oscillations near discontinuities (dispersive)

entry: Multigrid methods (MG methods), a group of algorithms for solving differential equations using a hierarchy of discretiza

bit.name: smooth on the fine grid, correct from coarser grids
bit.mechanism: a few relaxation sweeps on the fine grid remove the rapidly varying error; the remaining residual is transferred to a coarser grid where the slowly varying error is cheap to solve (recursively), the coarse correction is interpolated back and added, and a final smoothing sweep cleans the interpolation
requires: a hierarchy of grids with transfer operators
a smoother that kills high-frequency error
fails_when: anisotropic or non-elliptic operators defeat the smoother/coarse split

bit.name: emit digits of a constant one at a time from a bounded carry state
bit.mechanism: represent the constant as a series in a mixed-radix form, keep only the current remainders of each term, and at each step multiply through by the output base and carry to release the next digit; earlier digits are never stored or reused
requires: a series with rational terms for the constant
fails_when: quadratic in the digit count for the classic form

bit.name: evaluate a rational series by recursively halving the term range
bit.mechanism: split the range of terms in half, compute for each half an exact triple (product of denominators, product of numerators, partial sum numerator) recursively, and combine the two triples with a few big multiplications; one division at the end
requires: rational terms
fast big-integer multiplication
fails_when: irrational or non-hypergeometric terms

bit.name: iterate the arithmetic and geometric means to their common limit
bit.mechanism: replace a pair of numbers by their arithmetic mean and their geometric mean; the two converge quadratically to a common value, and a running correction term built from their squared differences yields the constant
requires: a square root at full precision each round
fails_when: each round needs full-precision arithmetic; no partial digits until the end

bit.name: carry the rounding error of each addition into the next
bit.mechanism: after adding a term to the running sum, recover what was lost to rounding by subtracting back, and add that lost piece to the next term before it is summed; the error no longer grows with the number of terms
requires: rounding that is deterministic and recoverable by subtraction
fails_when: compilers that reassociate the arithmetic remove the correction

bit.name: bring down a digit and subtract the largest fitting multiple
bit.mechanism: from the most significant end, append the next digit of the dividend to the partial remainder, find the largest single digit whose multiple of the divisor fits, emit that digit and subtract; the remainder carries to the next position
requires: comparison and subtraction on the partial remainder
fails_when: one digit per step; quadratic in length

bit.name: keep a negative remainder and add at the next step instead of restoring
bit.mechanism: subtract the divisor from the shifted remainder every step; if the result goes negative do not undo it -- emit a negative digit and ADD the divisor at the next step instead; a final fix-up converts the signed digits to an ordinary quotient
requires: a signed-digit quotient representation
fails_when: needs the final conversion step

bit.name: choose the quotient digit from a table on the leading bits, using a redundant digit set
bit.mechanism: look at only a few leading bits of the partial remainder and divisor and read the next quotient digit from a small table; because the digit set is redundant (includes negatives) a slightly wrong choice is corrected by later digits rather than by a comparison
requires: a digit-selection table (data) and a redundant digit set
fails_when: a wrong table entry gives systematically wrong results (the 1994 processor bug)

bit.name: scale numerator and denominator by a common factor that drives the denominator to one
bit.mechanism: multiply both numerator and denominator by the same factor (two minus the denominator) each round; the denominator converges quadratically to one and the numerator to the quotient; the two multiplications per round are independent and can run in parallel
requires: a denominator scaled into a fixed interval near one
fails_when: rounding errors accumulate (no self-correction, unlike the reciprocal-refinement route)

bit.name: step to the zero of the local linearisation
bit.mechanism: at the current guess, replace the function by its tangent line and jump to where that line crosses zero; repeat -- the error roughly squares each step once close
requires: a derivative at every guess
a starting guess in the basin
fails_when: divergence or cycling from a poor start; flat derivative

entry: Alpha max plus beta min algorithm

bit.name: approximate a norm by a weighted sum of the larger and smaller magnitudes
bit.mechanism: take the absolute values of the two components, scale the larger by one constant and the smaller by another, and add; the constants are chosen so the worst-case relative error over all angles is minimised
requires: two constants (data)
fails_when: error of a few percent; not a substitute where the exact norm matters

bit.name: square, and multiply in by the binary digits of the exponent
bit.mechanism: scan the exponent bit by bit; square the accumulator at every bit and multiply in the base only where the bit is set, so the number of multiplications is proportional to the bit length rather than the exponent
requires: an associative operation
fails_when: not minimal in multiplications; leaks the exponent through timing if data-dependent

bit.name: find a short chain of sums reaching the exponent, one multiplication per link
bit.mechanism: search for a sequence starting at one in which every element is the sum of two earlier elements and the last is the exponent; each link then costs one multiplication of already-computed powers, so a short chain gives a minimal-multiplication power
requires: a fixed exponent worth optimising for
fails_when: finding the shortest chain is hard; heuristics give near-minimal chains

bit.name: apply a fixed sequence of shrinking elementary steps, choosing each sign by the residual
bit.mechanism: a table holds the angle (or log) of each elementary factor whose tangent (or ratio) is a power of two; step through the table, at each entry rotating or scaling in whichever direction reduces the remaining target, using only shifts and adds; the accumulated direction bits and the residual give the function value
requires: a table of elementary angles or logs (data)
shift and add only
fails_when: one bit of precision per step; a final scale constant

bit.name: work in a scaled residue form so that reduction becomes a multiply and a shift
bit.mechanism: represent every residue multiplied by a power of the machine radix; then reducing a product modulo the odd modulus needs only a multiplication by a precomputed inverse and a shift, never a trial division; convert in once and out once
requires: an odd modulus
one precomputed inverse of the modulus modulo the radix
fails_when: a single operation is not cheaper; only a chain of them pays for the conversions

bit.name: recode runs of ones in the multiplier as one subtract and one add
bit.mechanism: scan adjacent pairs of multiplier bits; a run of ones contributes a subtraction of the multiplicand at its start and an addition at its end instead of one addition per bit, and the same rule handles negative two's-complement multipliers without a sign case
requires: two's-complement operands
fails_when: alternating bit patterns are the worst case (no runs)

bit.name: filter each projection, then smear it back along its rays
bit.mechanism: apply a ramp high-pass filter to each one-dimensional projection, then add each filtered projection back into the image along the rays that produced it; the filter cancels the blur that plain smearing would give
requires: projections at many angles
a one-dimensional filter
fails_when: few or noisy angles give streak artefacts

bit.name: represent a moving boundary as the zero level of an evolving field
bit.mechanism: instead of tracking boundary points, store a field over the whole grid whose zero contour is the boundary; evolve the field by a speed equation and read the boundary off wherever the field crosses zero, so merging and splitting need no special handling
requires: a grid over the whole domain
periodic re-initialisation to a distance field
fails_when: one dimension more storage than the boundary itself; the field drifts from a distance function
